critical_code_review_comments: public_commerce.py — Price resolution is server-side only (_price_for reads book.pricing.ebook_price with list_price fallback). Client cannot pass amount. GOOD.

public_commerce.py — /download/{session_id} rejects with 403 unless payment_status == 'paid' AND the record exists AND the book is still authorized AND the epub file is on disk. Solid defense in depth.
public_commerce.py — Idempotent DB update uses {payment_status: {$ne: 'paid'}} guard so repeated status polls cannot corrupt the record. GOOD.

QRUPurchaseSuccess.js — Polls /checkout/status every 2s up to 12 attempts (~24s). Good UX. Consider one final retry after 25s or a manual 'I paid — check again' button in case Stripe webhooks are slower than 24s; not blocking for MVP.

MINOR — QRUBookPage price display uses `book.currency === 'USD' ? '$' : ''`. If a future non-USD currency is set the price loses its symbol entirely. Consider Intl.NumberFormat with currency for future-proofing (post-MVP).

MINOR — publicApi.js has no retry/backoff on transient failures; on flaky preview networks the featured grid could show 'no titles' briefly. Small resilience improvement (react-query, or a single retry) would smooth this. Not blocking.
